clue.text: Spanish chap in bedroom penetrates

indicators.note: the bedroom piece pushes its way into the middle of the word for in

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
BR is the usual estate-agent abbreviation for bedroom

explanation.surface: Something faintly scandalous about a Spaniard getting into someone's bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a link word here: it gives HOME, which BR then penetrates.
explanation.definitionFit: Hombre is the Spanish word for a man, used in English slang for a fellow.

clue.text: Moulding American's expression of surprise

definitions.meaning: an S-shaped architectural moulding, double curved
...! is an American exclamation of surprise

explanation.definitionFit: An ogee is a double-curved moulding, and 'O gee' is a Yankee exclamation of astonishment.

clue.text: Spooner's taken charge of salt water subsistence level

indicators.note: Dr Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two pieces trade their starts

parts.note: someone who has taken charge has led
brine is salt water

explanation.surface: An odd image of someone running a saltwater supply at bare survival level.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of LED BRINE gives 'bred line', which sounds like the answer; the swap goes by sound, so 'bred' is spelt BREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Living on the breadline means existing at the poorest level of subsistence.

clue.text: Name-dropping what's not oddly male or female

indicators.note: the N for name falls further down the word, to its end

parts.note: what is done not oddly is done evenly

explanation.surface: A jibe at a name-dropper whose talk is a little odd, followed by a question about gender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name-dropping' looks like the social vice; it tells you to move the N in EVENLY down to the bottom of this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn is a given name borne by both men (Evelyn Waugh) and women.

clue.text: Two-hour shift revealed by shadow on timepiece

parts.note: to shadow someone is to dog them, follow closely
a watch is a timepiece

explanation.surface: A sundial-like image of a shadow on a clock revealing someone's shift.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogwatch is one of the two short two-hour watches at sea, 16:00 to 20:00 split in half.

clue.text: Imitate Cockney while designing this particular grid?

definitions.meaning: Cockneys famously leave out the h sound at the start of words
this grid's across entries are built so that many begin with H, which the setter has to omit or keep track of

explanation.definitionFit: Cockney speech is known for leaving off the h sound, the habit the phrase names.

clue.text: Light white china for holiday collectors (US)

parts.note: Goss china is white crested souvenir porcelain, collected by British holidaymakers since Victorian times
Amer. is an abbreviation for American, so US

explanation.surface: A remark about American tourists who collect light white china on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: GOSS is W.H. Goss's crested white souvenir china, sold at British seaside resorts and widely collected.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossamer means something extremely light and delicate, like a cobweb thread.

clue.text: Consent to a European donating £1,000

indicators.note: giving away means the thousand is removed from the word

parts.note: a Greek is a European
K stands for a thousand, as in a grand

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to let a European donate a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to consent or give one's assent.

clue.text: Top expert holds comic actor up to qualify

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid

indicators.note: the top and expert pieces together hold the actor inside them

parts.note: an ace is an expert

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the actor's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Jacques Tati was the French comic actor of Monsieur Hulot

explanation.surface: A top expert holding up a comic actor so he can qualify.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the actor's name, since in a down light it is read from the bottom; the result sits inside CAP + ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To capacitate is to make capable, to qualify someone for a role.

clue.text: Something undesirable has started: lion's feasting on sheep and half a horse

indicators.note: the hero piece eats, wraps round, the sheep and horse pieces

parts.note: a lion, a celebrated brave person, is a hero; the 's is has
a ewe is a sheep

indicators.note: only the first of the two letters is kept, half the horse word

parts.note: gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: A lion devouring a sheep and half a horse: something nasty has begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lion' is a hero here, not LEO.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Here we go' is the weary idiom said when something unwelcome is starting again.

clue.text: Angel cuts back on hydrogen

indicators.note: the cutting word is read backwards

parts.note: to pare is to cut
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A celestial being reduces its hydrogen intake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses PARES to SERAP; 'on' just joins H at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraph is one of the highest order of angels.

clue.text: Time to seize a head in Florida

parts.note: a day is a time or period
to nab is to seize
per head, as in five pounds a head, is each

explanation.surface: Time to grab someone in Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a head' means each, as in a price per person; the definition is the location of the place.
explanation.definitionFit: Daytona Beach is a city on the Atlantic coast of Florida, famous for motor racing.

clue.text: Soldier to sleep all right in luxury, an unknown commitment

indicators.note: the soldier, sleep and all-right pieces go inside the luxury word

parts.note: pie, as in pie in the sky, stands for a treat or luxury
GI is an American soldier
a nap is a sleep
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A soldier nodding off in comfort, signing up for something without knowing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To buy a pig in a poke is to commit to something without seeing it first.

clue.text: Reproduction of sound poem in corner square

indicators.note: the poem sits inside the square's name

parts.note: h1 is a corner square of a chessboard
If is Rudyard Kipling's famous poem

explanation.surface: A poem tucked away in the corner of a square.
explanation.walkthrough: Chess notation names squares by file letter and rank number, so h1 is a corner square.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-fi, high fidelity, is equipment for faithful reproduction of recorded sound.

clue.text: Still, two ducks get devoured by the wild canine

indicators.note: the still and ducks pieces go inside the rearranged word
the word the is run wild, its letters rearranged

parts.note: still means yet
a duck is a score of nought, O, so two ducks are OO

explanation.surface: Two ducks eaten by a wild canine animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' makes ETH from THE, which devours YETOO; 'canine' is the tooth, not a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye tooth is a canine tooth, below the eye in the upper jaw.

clue.text: Demands here what Moneypenny provides?

definitions.meaning: a document on which requests for goods are written
in the Bond films Miss Moneypenny is secretary to M, keeping his office organised for him

explanation.definitionFit: An order form is the sheet on which orders, demands for goods, are placed.

clue.text: It may appear to be the end for many soldiers

definitions.text: It may appear to be the end for many soldiers

parts.words: It may appear to be the end for many soldiers
parts.note: soldiers are the soldier ants, and the creature that eats them in quantity is their end

explanation.definitionFit: This mammal feeds on ants, including soldier ants, by the thousand.

clue.text: New immigrant to Hungary, Spain, Portugal and Ireland

parts.note: H is the international vehicle code for Hungary

indicators.note: the new piece enters the peninsula word as an immigrant would

parts.note: the Iberian peninsula, Iberia, comprises Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: A newcomer arrives in several European countries in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland.

clue.text: Does old Mrs Cotton hit it off?

parts.note: Dot Cotton was a long-running character in the BBC soap EastEnders

indicators.note: the word it is taken off the word hit

explanation.surface: Asking whether an elderly lady named Cotton gets along well with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Dot Cotton was the chain-smoking gossip of EastEnders, a London-set BBC TV soap; 'hit it off' looks like an idiom but means HIT without IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Doth is the archaic third-person form of the verb do.

clue.text: From soak, pungent-leaved plant's emerged in nursery

indicators.note: a soak is a drunkard, so this is the word as slurred from a drunk's mouth
the slurred word is what comes out when the drunk tries to say it

parts.note: cress is a salad plant with peppery leaves; the 's is has

explanation.surface: A peppery salad plant sprouting from a soaked tray in a plant nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soak' is a drunk, not a verb; a drunk slurs the S sounds of CRESS into SH, giving 'cresh', the sound of the answer. 'nursery' is a day nursery, not a garden centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A crèche is a day nursery where young children are minded.

clue.text: With this type of application you may renew capital growth

definitions.text: With this type of application you may renew capital growth

parts.words: With this type of application you may renew capital growth
parts.note: capital is the head and its growth is hair, so this is something rubbed on to bring back a bald scalp, not a finance form

explanation.definitionFit: This lotion is applied to the scalp to make lost hair grow back.

clue.text: Hurriedly build approach

definitions.meaning: to throw something up quickly, as a dress or a shed
the lead-up period or the sprint before a jump or delivery

explanation.definitionFit: To run up is to make quickly; a run-up is an approach, as before a jump.

clue.text: Wage slave takes a long time

indicators.note: the phrase takes, holds within it, the letters of the answer

explanation.surface: A worker on low pay takes ages to get anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages is an informal word for a very long time.

clue.text: Watford player's unusual other name?

definitions.note: the 's is a link meaning is

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement of the letters of other plus N

explanation.surface: A footballer for Watford has a strange alternative name.
explanation.walkthrough: Watford FC, an English football club, are nicknamed the Hornets.
explanation.definitionFit: Watford Football Club are nicknamed the Hornets, so a player is one of them.

clue.text: Unexpected hitch for sports body thought to have no time at all for touring

indicators.note: what is left goes round the sports body

indicators.text: to have no time at all
indicators.note: every T, standing for time, is removed from thought

parts.note: the ICC is the International Cricket Council

explanation.surface: A sports body thought too busy to tour suffers an unexpected setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have no time at all' means every T goes, not just one; ICC is world cricket's governing body.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiccough, or hiccup, is a minor setback or unexpected snag.

clue.text: "Evening Star" this fellow's getting to read? Not quite all of it

parts.note: he's is this fellow is

indicators.note: the last letter of the reading word is dropped

parts.note: to peruse is to read

explanation.surface: A man settling down to read the Evening Star newspaper, but not the whole thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesperus is the evening star, the planet Venus seen after sunset.

clue.text: Get someone involved in the Net?

definitions.text: Get someone involved in the Net?

parts.words: Get someone involved in the Net?
parts.note: to catch someone up as if in a fishing net or web, rather than the internet

explanation.definitionFit: To enmesh someone is to entangle them, as in a net.
